Subject: OrionBank — Data residency & region pinning follow-up

Hi Samira / Tom,

Great to meet you both on the call earlier — thanks for taking the time. Quick recap and a few follow-up questions so we can scope the technical proposal and next steps.

Call recap (high level)
- Requirement: EU-only processing and storage for customer PII and transcripts for retail banking product lines.
- Retention: Some lines require retention up to 7 years; others shorter.
- Failover: You want automatic failover for availability but only within EU, and strict control over any cross-region replication.

Follow-up questions (to confirm):
1) Data residency boundaries: For the transcripts and token-level logs (request/response), do you require that both processing and cold backups remain physically in EU at all times (no cross-region replication), or is cross-region backup allowed if encrypted and customer-approved?
2) Logs & PII in telemetry: Do you need PII redaction/masking at the platform level (i.e., Redwood suppresses PII before logs leave the node), or is it sufficient to configure log retention and forward sanitized logs to your customer-owned storage?
3) Retention windows: Can you share the retention windows per product line (retail chat, internal support, fraud ops)? We'll map those to retention policies in the proposal.
4) Disaster recovery: Is an active-active cross-region DR unacceptable, or would you consider active-passive where failover is triggered only by a declared DR event and controlled via a policy?

Attachments: I attached our standard SOC2 questionnaire that we discussed — orionbank-soc2-questions.pdf (answers to a subset are in progress).

Next steps
- If you can reply with answers to the four bullets above, Marissa (copied) can put together an implementation option set (Hosted EU, Dedicated EU, Private deployment) with implications for backups, failover, and cost.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-45 minute technical deep dive next week to walk the architecture and get to a draft SOW.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: OrionBank — Data residency & region pinning follow-up

Hi Aditya — thanks for the summary. Quick answers from our side:

1) Data residency: For regulated retail and payments pipelines we require processing and storage to remain within the EU (ideally Ireland and/or Frankfurt). Cross-region replication is only permitted for DR under explicit contractual terms; by default, backups must be kept in-region.
2) Logs & PII: We need PII removed from platform telemetry. Ideally Redwood can provide PII suppression rules (name, account number, email) at the ingestion layer. Forwarding sanitized logs to our S3 is acceptable as a secondary control.
3) Retention windows: Retail chat — 2 years; Payments dispute conversations — 7 years; Internal support — 1 year.
4) Disaster recovery: Active-active across regions is not acceptable. Active-passive with a documented failover playbook is OK, but failover must be triggered only by our ops or by an agreed policy.

Outstanding questions for Redwood:
- Do you support region pinning per-customer or per-route? We prefer per-customer at the account level.
- For backups, what encryption and key management options are available (customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM?)
- Does Redwood offer on-prem / private-cloud deployment for fully air-gapped needs?

Happy to jump on a technical call. Tom and I are available Mon/Tue next week mornings CET.

Thanks,
Samira Qureshi
Head of Platform Risk | OrionBank
samira.qureshi@orionbank.com

Subject: Re: OrionBank — Data residency & region pinning follow-up

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear answers. I pulled in Vanessa (solutions lead for dedicated/private deployments) and sketched the options below.

Short answers to your outstanding questions:
- Region pinning: Supported per-customer (account-level) and can be applied per-route as needed. Default is account-level for strict residency.
- KM options: We support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers and can integrate with HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. Backups can be encrypted with CMKs and, by default, kept in-region. Cross-region replication can be configured but requires approval and contract-level controls.
- Private/on-prem: Yes — Private deployment (VPC or on-prem package) is available and is the recommended path for customers that require air-gapped or contractual EU-only guarantees.

Architecture & failover (brief):
- Hosted EU (fastest): Requests routed exclusively to EU hosts (Ireland/FRA). Backups kept in-region; cross-region replication disabled by default.
- Dedicated EU (reserved capacity): Same residency guarantees as Hosted but with isolated GPU pools and optional dedicated network links. Snapshots stored in EU.
- Private deployment: Customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem — no cross-region replication unless you explicitly enable it.

Failover modes:
- Active-passive (recommended for strict residency): Primary in-region; passive standby can be configured in-region. Cross-region passive standby possible but only with contractual approval.
- Active-active: Not recommended for EU-only mandates (would require cross-region processing).

PII & logs:
- We offer platform-level suppression rules (configurable regex/PII detectors) that redact fields before they are written to telemetry.
- Audit logs can be streamed to customer-owned S3/GCS buckets inside your account for long-term retention and for regulatory audit. Retention policies are configurable per dataset.

Attachments: I've attached a simple region diagram that shows how Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments can be configured to meet your constraints — region-architecture-diagram.png (image/png, 210KB). Also linking the product doc for region pinning below.

Next steps
1) Technical deep dive (30-45m) — Tue 13 Apr, 09:00-10:00 CET works for our team.
2) We will prepare two artifacts for you: (a) a short implementation options memo (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) with cost delta, and (b) a draft SOW for a Private deployment option.

Let me know if there are any other constraints (certifications, encryption-at-rest details) you'd like included.

Best,
Marissa Cole
